rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at moderate temperature to ensure all 6 compounds elute within 42 min and reveal the overall elution window and any critical pairs. The wide phi range and mid-length gradient maximize information while avoiding an obviously truncated run.

All pairs are already fully resolved, so the objective is now to cut time aggressively while keeping all peaks inside the gradient. This narrower, steeper window should pull the first peak later from the near-void region and bring the last peak much closer to 10 min without risking truncation.

We already have the maximum CRF, so now probe whether the gradient can be shortened further while maintaining all pair resolutions at or above 1.5 and keeping the last peak within 10 min. This is the cleanest one-step time reduction around the current optimum.

Resolution margins remain very large, so shorten the gradient another step to find where the first critical pair approaches the 1.5 threshold. This keeps the same selectivity while pushing for the fastest fully resolved method.

The method is still far from the resolution limit, so reduce tG one more step to continue bracketing the fastest possible fully resolved gradient. Keeping phi0, phi1, and T fixed isolates the effect of slope on the current worst pair.

The current worst pair still has comfortable margin above 1.5, so test the shortest available gradient to see if full resolution is retained. This directly checks whether the grid minimum tG is already sufficient for a maximal-CRF method.

At tG = 2 min only the first pair fails, so target that region by lowering phi0 to give the earliest compounds more retention and separation while keeping the run extremely short. This tests whether reshaping the front of the gradient can recover full resolution at the minimum gradient time.

Lowering phi0 worsened the first pair, so probe the opposite direction: a higher phi0 with the same 2 min gradient may shift the earliest pair into a more favorable part of the ramp. This efficiently tests whether the limiting pair is controlled more by the front-end solvent window than by slope alone.

Raising phi0 improved the limiting first pair at tG = 2 min, so continue in that direction to see whether it can cross the 1.5 threshold while preserving the very short run. This is the most direct next test on the apparent trend.

The first-pair resolution at tG = 2 min has improved as phi0 increased from 0.10 to 0.25, so take one more step higher to test whether it finally reaches full credit. This continues the clear trend while staying within a safe scouting envelope for the rest of the peaks.

At tG = 2 min, phi0 = 0.25 was the best front-end setting so far; now narrow the gradient window from the top to make the slope shallower and potentially recover the remaining first-pair resolution without lengthening the run. This targets the only failing pair while keeping all compounds in a very short method.

Narrowing the upper end from 0.75 to 0.70 improved the limiting first pair at tG = 2 min, so continue one more step to make the gradient still shallower and test whether it reaches R ≥ 1.5. The last peak remains far from any time penalty, so there is room to spend a bit more retention on resolution.

The 2 min, 0.25–0.65 method is essentially at the resolution threshold, so use temperature as the gentlest selectivity lever to try to push the first pair cleanly above R = 1.5 while retaining the same short gradient. A small decrease in T should slightly increase retention and can improve a marginal front-end pair without threatening the 10 min limit.

Now that full resolution is achieved at the shortest gradient, step temperature down once more to map how much margin the critical first pair gains and confirm robustness of this ultrafast method. The run is still comfortably below the 10 min threshold, so this is a low-risk refinement around the new optimum.

With full resolution established at 0.25–0.65, test a slightly narrower window to see whether the first pair stays above 1.5 while trimming the gradient to the observed elution range. Using 35 C preserves some safety margin versus 40 C but should keep the run comfortably under 10 min.

The narrower 0.25–0.60 window still gives full resolution, so raise temperature to recover some speed while checking whether the first pair remains above the 1.5 threshold. This is the most direct way to see if a faster version of the narrowed-window method can also achieve the maximum CRF.

The 0.25–0.60, 2 min method at 40 C still has some margin on the critical first pair, so raise T one step to see whether an even faster, hotter version preserves full resolution. This efficiently brackets the upper temperature limit for the shortest successful gradient window found so far.

At the promising 0.25–0.60, 2 min, 40 C method the first pair is only moderately above threshold, so lower phi0 one step to test whether the front-end selectivity improves while keeping the same short window and temperature. This maps whether the 0.25 setting is truly optimal for the limiting pair in the narrowed gradient.

Lowering phi0 from 0.25 to 0.20 improved the critical first pair in the 0.60 upper-window method, so test 0.15 next to locate the best front-end setting. This may deliver a more robust fully resolved 2 min method while still keeping the last peak well below 10 min.

Among the 2 min, phi1 = 0.60 methods, phi0 = 0.20 gave the strongest margin at 40 C; lowering T one step should further strengthen the critical first pair and test a robust best-in-region condition. This helps identify the safest ultrafast method among the many CRF-equal candidates.

The 0.20–0.60, 2 min method looks strongest so far for the critical pair, so lower T one more step to confirm the robustness ceiling before approaching the 10 min boundary. This will identify whether additional selectivity gain is still available without incurring any time penalty.

The 0.20–0.60, 2 min, 40 C method already achieves full resolution with some margin, so trim phi1 one more step to see whether the gradient can be tightened further while staying under the 10 min last-peak limit. This is the most direct remaining way to improve the ultrafast method without lengthening tG.

The 0.20–0.55, 2 min method only misses maximum CRF because the last peak is just over 10 min, while resolution is comfortably sufficient. Raising T one step should pull the last peak back under 10 min, and this run directly tests whether that tighter window can also achieve CRF 1.000.

The 0.20–0.55, 2 min, 45 C method reaches CRF 1.000 but the critical pair is close to the threshold, so lower phi0 one step to test whether the front-end resolution can be improved while maintaining the tighter gradient window and sub-10 min last peak. This is a focused robustness optimization around the fastest successful window.

With one injection left, test the opposite side of phi0 around the successful 0.20–0.55, 45 C condition to see whether the critical first pair gains margin in the tightest window that still gives CRF 1.000. This final run best brackets the true front-end optimum for the fastest successful method.
